run.notes: Sample of what steps 7 and 8 hand to Phase 4, built from the Veloran reference report v1.0 (a synthetic case). Base hours and costs are the report's; the low and high hour ranges are illustrative until step 8 supplies real ones.

sources.loaded_hourly_rate: Average salary $118,000 x 1.30 for benefits and payroll taxes, plus $19,400 overhead per person, divided by 1,920 working hours (Veloran finance, FY2025)
sources.working_weeks_per_year: 52 weeks minus PTO and holidays (Veloran handbook)
sources.adoption_rate: Conservative planning assumption (70%), applied to every saving; 50% and 85% for the low and high cases

formulas.hours_saved_per_week: effect share x hours lost per week, rounded to whole hours
formulas.annual_time_savings: hours saved x working weeks x loaded hourly rate x adoption
formulas.annual_deal_margin: deals lost x recovery share x adoption x average deal value x contribution margin
formulas.year_one_cost: upfront cost + first year of ongoing cost
formulas.mix_of_fixes: largest saving + each other saving x (1 - overlap); never more than the cap share of hours lost
formulas.choice: highest first-year net benefit among eligible mixes that pay back within the limit

bottlenecks.name: Staffing blind spots: unplanned bench time and last-minute assignments
root_causes: No forward view of capacity: the staffing sheet tracks current bookings only
Sales and delivery plan separately: start dates live in CRM opportunities the staffing sheet never reads
Bench time has no default use

options.label: Option 1: AI forecasting agent
options.name: AI forecasting agent
options.how_it_solves: An agent in the firm's own CRM predicts roll-offs and demand from pipeline and booking history, then proposes staffing moves for a person to approve
example_vendors: Agentforce in the firm's own Salesforce org

effort.note: High: needs 12+ months of clean staffing data

governance.note: Medium: reads pipeline and staff data; every move needs human sign-off
governance.data_accessed: Pipeline, bookings and skills (internal; personnel data)
go_live_gates: Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy
A named person signs off every staffing move the agent proposes

risks_and_dependencies: Forecasts are only as good as the staffing history behind them
options.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 1
options.status_reason: Deferred: an AI forecast needs at least 12 months of clean booking data (current: 0). The recommended PSA tool creates this; revisit once the PSA holds 12 months of bookings.

trace.hours_saved_per_week: 0.349 share x 129 h lost = 45.02 -> 45 h a week
trace.annual_time_savings: 45 h x 48 weeks x $90 x 70% adoption = $136,080

options.label: Option 2: PSA tool
options.name: PSA tool
options.how_it_solves: One system holds bookings, roll-offs, skills and pipeline demand on a single timeline, eight weeks out

effort.note: Medium: data migration and new habits for 50 people

risks_and_dependencies: Must sync with the CRM and replace the current time tool
options.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 2

trace.hours_saved_per_week: 0.465 share x 129 h lost = 59.99 -> 60 h a week
trace.annual_time_savings: 60 h x 48 weeks x $90 x 70% adoption = $181,440

options.label: Option 3: Capacity council and bench-to-certification
options.name: Capacity council and bench-to-certification
options.how_it_solves: A 30-minute weekly meeting books the next eight weeks; any unbooked day defaults to a certification plan or a reusable asset

effort.note: Low: one meeting and one rule

risks_and_dependencies: Discipline; savings stall if leaders skip the meeting
options.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 3

trace.hours_saved_per_week: 0.233 share x 129 h lost = 30.06 -> 30 h a week
trace.annual_time_savings: 30 h x 48 weeks x $90 x 70% adoption = $90,720

options.reskilling_targets_note: Skill signals from step 2 are not available yet.

recommendation.together_note: The PSA makes capacity visible, the council turns it into decisions, and the certification rule gives every unplanned free day a use.
recommendation.summary: We recommend Option 3 (Capacity council and bench-to-certification) and Option 2 (PSA tool) together. The PSA makes capacity visible, the council turns it into decisions, and the certification rule gives every unplanned free day a use. Together they save an estimated 85 hours a week ($257,040 a year) for $58,600 in year one, a payback of 2.7 months.

bottlenecks.name: Status reporting repeated across four places and recurring meetings
bottlenecks.category_label: Status reporting repeated across tools and meetings
root_causes: No single system of record: three tools grew up in different teams
Meetings collect status instead of making decisions
Client reporting is hand-built in a bespoke format per client

options.name: AI meeting notes and status drafts

go_live_gates: Consent from every party before any call is recorded

Vendor review: no training on client data

options.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 1

bottlenecks.name: Timesheets rebuilt from memory at the end of the week
root_causes: Weekly deadline, daily work: nothing prompts entry while memory is fresh
Entry is fully manual: the time tool does not read calendars or the tracker
No visible link between timesheets and money

options.label: Option 1: AI-drafted timesheets
options.name: AI-drafted timesheets
options.how_it_solves: An app drafts each person's day from calendar, tracker and document activity; the person edits and submits. Drafts are visible only to the employee.

effort.note: Low: install plus a privacy briefing

governance.note: Medium: reads calendar and app activity. Mitigated by on-device processing, employee-only drafts and no manager access to raw activity
governance.data_accessed: Calendar titles, tracker activity, app and document names on the employee's laptop
go_live_gates: Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy
Security and contract review of the timesheet tool, including no-training terms
Drafts stay employee-only; managers never see raw activity

risks_and_dependencies: Must export to the PSA if one is chosen
options.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 3, Option 1

trace.hours_saved_per_week: 0.595 share x 42 h lost = 24.99 -> 25 h a week
trace.annual_time_savings: 25 h x 48 weeks x $90 x 70% adoption = $75,600

options.label: Option 2: PSA time module
options.name: PSA time module
options.how_it_solves: Time entry moves into the PSA chosen for staffing, next to bookings, with approvals in one place
example_vendors: Same vendor as the PSA tool
options.cost_note: $0 extra once the PSA tool is approved

implementation.label: Arrives with the PSA, weeks 6 to 8

risks_and_dependencies: Moves the same manual entry to a new screen

trace.annual_time_savings: 12 h x 48 weeks x $90 x 70% adoption = $36,288

options.label: Option 3: Daily time rule
options.name: Daily time rule
options.how_it_solves: Log time before leaving each day: a 4:30 p.m. chat nudge, a 15-minute end-of-day calendar block, and on-time rates shared by team, never by name
risks_and_dependencies: The habit fades without the nudge and team-level feedback
options.evidence: Veloran reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 3, Option 3

trace.hours_saved_per_week: 0.357 share x 42 h lost = 14.99 -> 15 h a week
trace.annual_time_savings: 15 h x 48 weeks x $90 x 70% adoption = $45,360
trace.payback_months: No year-one cost: pays back immediately

recommendation.together_note: The rule fixes when time is logged; the drafts fix the effort and the forgetting.
recommendation.summary: We recommend Option 3 (Daily time rule) and Option 1 (AI-drafted timesheets) together. The rule fixes when time is logged; the drafts fix the effort and the forgetting. Together they save an estimated 35 hours a week ($105,840 a year) for $11,120 in year one, a payback of 1.3 months.

program.summary: The 3 recommendations cost $79,520 in year one and save an estimated $589,680 a year, a combined payback of 1.6 months. From year two, ongoing costs are $37,920 a year and the net benefit is about $551,760 a year. At 70% adoption, the 195 gross hours become about 137 effective hours a week: 48% of the 283 hours lost to the bottlenecks in scope.
